s8-introduction-to-bit-manipulation-theo.trick: Use masks for individual bits: AND tests, OR sets, XOR toggles, and AND with an inverted mask clears. Positions are zero-based.

s8-check-if-the-i-th-bit-is-set-or-not.trick: Shift a one to zero-based position i and AND it with the number. Use an unsigned type to avoid signed-shift pitfalls.

s8-check-if-a-number-is-odd-or-not.trick: The least significant bit is 1 exactly when an integer is odd.

s8-check-if-a-number-is-power-of-2-or-no.trick: A positive power of two has exactly one set bit, which n & (n-1) clears.

s8-count-the-number-of-set-bits.trick: Repeatedly clear the rightmost set bit with n &= n-1. The loop runs once per set bit.
s8-count-the-number-of-set-bits.time: O(k), k = number of set bits

s8-set-unset-the-rightmost-unset-bit.trick: n | (n+1) sets the lowest zero bit; n & (n-1) clears the lowest one bit. Unsigned arithmetic makes overflow behavior defined.

s8-swap-two-numbers.trick: XOR swapping is a bitwise exercise: three XORs exchange values, but the alias check is essential. Prefer std::swap in production code.

s8-divide-two-integers-without-using-mul.trick: Subtract the largest shifted divisor that fits, from high bit to low bit. Compute magnitudes in 64-bit to handle INT_MIN safely.

s8-count-number-of-bits-to-be-flipped-to.trick: XOR marks positions where A and B differ. Count the set bits of that XOR.

s8-find-the-number-that-appears-odd-numb.trick: XOR cancels every value occurring an even number of times, leaving the one odd-frequency value.

s8-power-set.trick: Each bitmask from 0 to 2^n-1 describes one subset: bit i says whether to include element i.

s8-find-xor-of-numbers-from-l-to-r.trick: XOR from 0 through n follows a four-value cycle depending on n mod 4. XOR of L..R is prefix(R) XOR prefix(L-1).

s8-find-the-two-numbers-appearing-odd-nu.trick: XOR all values to get a^b. Isolate one bit where a and b differ and XOR the two resulting groups separately.

s8-print-prime-factors-of-a-number.trick: Try divisors only up to the remaining number's square root. Record each prime divisor once, divide out all copies, then append any remaining prime.
s8-print-prime-factors-of-a-number.space: O(k) output, k = distinct prime factors

s8-all-divisors-of-a-number.trick: Each divisor d up to sqrt(n) pairs with n/d. Avoid duplicating the square root, then sort the answer.
s8-all-divisors-of-a-number.time: O(√n + d log d), d = number of divisors

s8-sieve-of-eratosthenes.trick: Start with all numbers at least 2 marked prime. For each prime p up to sqrt(n), mark its multiples starting at p².

s8-find-prime-factorisation-of-a-number-.trick: Precompute the smallest prime factor (SPF) of every value up to n. Repeatedly divide by SPF[n] to list prime factors with multiplicity.
s8-find-prime-factorisation-of-a-number-.time: O(n log log n) preprocessing, O(log n) factorization

s8-power-n-x.trick: Use binary exponentiation: multiply the answer for each set bit of the nonnegative exponent, squaring the base after every bit.
